methodologyNotes: 12 notable popcorn machines selected as the 2026 buyer-comparison set, spanning stirring-oil, hot-air, retro tabletop-kettle, commercial cart-style, manual stovetop, and microwave designs. Seeds from the brief were verified and corrected: 'Nostalgia RKP730' does not exist in any retailer or manufacturer catalog searched — the real, currently-sold Nostalgia retro kettle popper is the RKP630 (2.5oz kettle), included in its place. 'Whirley Pop Stovetop' and 'Wabash Valley Farms Whirley' are the SAME product (Whirley-Pop is Wabash Valley Farms' trademarked stovetop popper line) and were consolidated into one entry (the classic 6-qt aluminum Original Whirley-Pop, confirmed on wfarms.com — Wabash Valley Farms' current site; wabashvalleyfarms.com now redirects there). Cuisinart CPM-100 (EasyPop) is confirmed discontinued directly by Cuisinart, but is retained as a widely-compared/still-purchasable-via-retailer unit (Amazon/Best Buy), per standard practice for recently-discontinued but still-relevant models; price reflects current Best Buy retail, not original MSRP. Two Presto units (PopLite 04820 and the Orville Redenbacher's-branded 04821) are functionally the identical 1475W hot-air popper sold under two brandings/colorways at the same $42.99 gopresto.com price — both are real, separately-merchandised SKUs buyers actively compare, so both are kept as distinct entries with the duplication noted here rather than hidden. 'Superior Popcorn Company' is a private-label commercial-cart brand distributed across Wayfair/Walmart/Lowe's/Amazon rather than through its own manufacturer site (no superiorpopcorncompany.com domain resolves); its specs (8oz kettle, 850W, tempered-glass cabinet, old-maids reject-kernel drawer) are corroborated identically across at least three independent retail listings, but a single authoritative price could not be pinned to one exact SKU this pass, so priceUsd is null rather than guessed. Primary sources fetched directly where access allowed: westbend.com, gopresto.com (x2), wfarms.com, target.com (Great Northern listing), thepopcornmachine.com (Great Northern Matinee listing), golfcresthardware.com (Nostalgia RKP630 UPC-verified listing). Several manufacturer/retailer sites (bydash.com, shopelitegourmet.com, ecolutionhome.com, Walmart, Amazon, Wayfair, Lowe's) returned bot-blocking errors (403/429/500) throughout this research pass despite repeated attempts at different times; for the three products this affected most (Dash DAPP150V2, Elite Gourmet EPM-250, Ecolution Micro-Pop) specs are drawn from multiply-corroborated retailer/manual listings but priceUsd is left null rather than reported from a single unverified snippet. West Bend Stir Crazy wattage is reported as 850W per westbend.com's own product title, though several third-party retail listings (Kmart, Bonanza) list 1000W for the same SKU — flagged, not resolved, since the manufacturer figure is authoritative. Nostalgia RKP630 wattage shows a similar split (300W per one aggregator vs 370W per the UPC-matched golfcresthardware listing); 370W is used as the more specifically-sourced figure. capacity_qt is normalized to quarts for comparability (cup/oz/gallon figures converted: 4 cups = 1 qt, 1 gal = 4 qt) with the manufacturer's original unit preserved in each product's provenance field. accessedAt 2026-08-01 on all entries.

products.name: West Bend Stir Crazy Electric Popcorn Popper (82505)
products.priceNote: US MSRP $44.99 per westbend.com official product page. Frequently discounted to $30-40 at Walmart/other retailers.

specs.material: Plastic housing with triple-layer aluminum heating plate and motorized stir rod

products.provenance: westbend.com product page (fetched directly) confirms model 82505, 850W, 6-quart capacity (fully pops up to 6.75 qt in ~4 min), 13"W x 10"L x 10"H, triple-layer heating plate, motorized stir rod with automatic reversal, includes serving bowl lid, and lists $44.99 as the regular price (item shown out of stock direct but sold at major retailers). Amazon listing (B00KL8SM92) corroborates 6-quart capacity, red color, stirring rod, and serving bowl. Some third-party listings (Kmart, Bonanza) report 1000W instead of 850W for the same model — the manufacturer's own 850W figure is used here. No measuring cup or dishwasher-safety claim found in manufacturer copy, so both left null rather than guessed. Photo is Wikimedia Commons' CC BY-SA 3.0 image of an earlier West Bend Stir Crazy unit (same product line/design), uploaded by user Royalbroil in 2013.
